prediction_ref.short_label: Humanoid whole-body control adopts force-aware contact evaluation by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary:
The Technical University of Munich's ThorArena benchmark is the origin signal for this prediction: it stress-tests humanoid whole-body control under deliberate, load-bearing contact rather than collision avoidance, replaying synchronized human motion-and-force demonstrations in simulation and scoring policies with a Force-Aware Tracking Score that grades tracking accuracy, robustness across force levels, control effort, and whether the robot stays upright to the end of the episode.
The headline finding directly motivates the forecast: force-informed evaluation exposes large performance gaps that stay invisible under conventional no-force testing, and only the authors' own Thor2 policy held near-perfect balance across all six contact-rich chores. With Figure, Agility, and Boston Dynamics pushing humanoids into factories where a person leans on and hands things to the robot, this is the single academic benchmark whose method the prediction expects to cross into commercial or independent practice by H1 2027.

reference_links.label: arXiv - ThorArena: Benchmarking Humanoid Physical Interaction with Human Motion-Force Demonstrations
TechXplore - New test measures how well humanoid robots handle real-world forces

bridge.narrative: The ThorArena benchmark is the observed precondition this forecast names: it scores humanoid whole-body control under deliberate load-bearing contact and shows force-aware evaluation exposes balance failures invisible to conventional no-force testing. A concrete, reproducible method now exists for others to adopt.
bridge.remaining_gap: Only the authors' own policy passed; no independent lab or vendor has adopted the method yet.

prediction_ref.short_label: AI coding assistants make symlink-aware write consent the default by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary:
Wiz Research's July 8 GhostApproval disclosure is the origin signal: a malicious repository ships a file with a benign name such as project_settings.json that is actually a symlink to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, so when a developer approves what looks like a harmless config edit the write lands on the SSH file and plants an attacker's key for passwordless remote access. The core failure is a consent bypass - the approval dialog shows only the innocuous filename, never the resolved destination.
The six-vendor split is the forecast's forcing function: Amazon Q Developer (CVE-2026-12958), Cursor (CVE-2026-50549), and Google Antigravity shipped fixes, Augment and Windsurf were unpatched at disclosure, and Anthropic disputed that Claude Code's behavior is a bug. Once half the field carrying assigned CVEs treats silent symlink-following as a defect, the prediction is that most of the six converge on a write-approval prompt that resolves and shows the real target path before a developer okays an edit, by H1 2027.

bridge.narrative: GhostApproval showed the approval dialog hides a symlink's real target, letting an okayed edit plant an SSH key. Three of six assistants already shipped fixes that resolve and surface the true path, the observed precondition for the field converging on symlink-aware write consent.
bridge.remaining_gap: Two vendors stayed unpatched and Anthropic disputes the defect; not yet a shared default.
